subject: mathematics_2b
question_text: Find the parametric equations of the circle x² + y² − 6x + 4y − 12 = 0.

insider_note: The parametric form is nothing more than centre plus radius times cosine and sine, so the whole answer is the centre and the radius written into two lines.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Centre and radius
steps.margin_note: One mark. c = −12, so −c adds 12 and the radius is whole.
steps.why: The parametric equations are built from the centre and the radius alone, so both are read off first.

steps.label: Write the parametric equations
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Write θ in the answer; a parametric form without its parameter is incomplete.
steps.memory_tip: x = −g + r cos θ and y = −f + r sin θ. Centre first, then radius times cosine or sine.
lines: x = −g + r cos θ,  y = −f + r sin θ

lines.text: ∴ x = 3 + 5 cos θ,  y = −2 + 5 sin θ

steps.why: A point on the circle is the centre shifted by r in the direction θ. The horizontal shift is r cos θ and the vertical shift is r sin θ, which is why the centre coordinates appear untouched in front.
common_mistakes: Writing x = 3 cos θ and y = −2 sin θ, which drops the radius.
